Log to a time-stamped rotating file

Source: R/Appender.R
AppenderFileRotatingTime.Rd

An extension of AppenderFile that rotates logfiles based on certain conditions. Please refer to the documentation of rotor::rotate_time() for the meanings of the extra arguments

See also

AppenderFileRotatingDate, AppenderFileRotating, rotor::rotate()

Other Appenders: Appender, AppenderBuffer, AppenderConsole, AppenderFile, AppenderFileRotating, AppenderFileRotatingDate, AppenderTable

Super classes

Filterable -> Appender -> AppenderFile -> AppenderFileRotating -> AppenderFileRotatingTime

Active bindings

age

The maximum age of the log file that triggers rotation. See $set_age().

overwrite

Whether an existing backup for the same timestamp may be overwritten. See $set_overwrite().

fmt

The strftime()-style timestamp format used for naming backups. See $set_fmt().

cache_backups

TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE (the default) the list of backups is cached, if FALSE it is read from disk every time this appender triggers. Caching brings a significant speedup for checking whether to rotate or not based on the age of the last backup, but is only safe if there are no other programs/functions (except this appender) interacting with the backups.

AppenderFileRotatingTime$new()

Create a new AppenderFileRotatingTime.

Usage

AppenderFileRotatingTime$new(
  file,
  threshold = NA_integer_,
  layout = LayoutFormat$new(),
  filters = NULL,
  age = Inf,
  size = -1,
  max_backups = Inf,
  compression = FALSE,
  backup_dir = dirname(file),
  fmt = "%Y-%m-%d--%H-%M-%S",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  cache_backups = TRUE,
  create_file = NULL
)

Arguments

file

character scalar. Path to the log file. If file does not exist it will be created.

threshold

character or integer scalar. The minimum log level that triggers this Appender. See log_levels.

layout

A Layout that determines how LogEvents are formatted before being output by this Appender.

filters

A list of EventFilters or predicate functions used to filter events for this Appender. See Filterable.

age, size, max_backups, compression, backup_dir, fmt, overwrite, cache_backups

see rotor::rotate_time() for the meaning of these arguments. Note that backup_dir corresponds to dir.

create_file

Defunct, do not use.

AppenderFileRotatingTime$rotate()

Rotate the log file if it meets the rotation conditions (see $size, $age), or unconditionally if force = TRUE. See rotor::rotate_time() for details.

Usage

AppenderFileRotatingTime$rotate(force = FALSE, now = Sys.time())

Arguments

force

TRUE or FALSE. Force rotation regardless of whether the rotation conditions are met.

now

A POSIXct scalar. The timestamp to use for naming the new backup and for evaluating $age.

AppenderFileRotatingTime$set_age()

Set the maximum age of the log file that triggers rotation. See rotor::rotate_time().

Usage

AppenderFileRotatingTime$set_age(x)

Arguments

x

A difftime or numeric scalar (interpreted as days), or Inf to disable age-based rotation.
